cases.incident: Production exposed a healthy Qwen 1.7B original-voice worker and enabled expressive configuration, but Discord voice responses still called only the standard Piper synthesizer.
cases.invariant: When the attested expressive provider is ready, every safe Discord response segment is synthesized by Qwen 1.7B with the planned expression and original-recording voice profile; Piper is used only for natural speech when the expressive provider is unavailable.
cases.productionSignal: Provider class, attested model/profile/quantization identity, style, intensity bucket, segment index, completion outcome, and audio byte-count bucket without transcript, response text, audio, or user identifier.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A ready expressive provider is bypassed, a non-natural expression is flattened through Piper, the returned worker identity differs from the approved Qwen 1.7B x-vector profile, any intended segment is missing, or empty audio is delivered.

cases.incident: The production 1.7B worker used the named female Sohee voice and a 96-token cap instead of the listener-approved original-recording speaker identity, causing the wrong voice and truncated multi-sentence playback.
cases.invariant: Production runs on zeze with the attested 1.7B Base x-vector-only profile derived from original recordings, never the Sohee named speaker, and permits at least 192 audio tokens for complete multi-sentence playback.
cases.productionSignal: Attested model ID, quantization identity, voice profile, embedding digest, generated duration, EOS status, and segment count without raw voice data or conversation text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The worker reports a different model/profile/embedding identity, emits the Sohee voice, truncates an intended sentence, fails to reach EOS within the bounded generation window, or runs on land in production.

cases.incident: Discord users had no secure way to bind their Gahyeon identity to the shared ZezeStudio account, and the first ZezeStudio rollout failed startup because its multi-constructor link service did not identify the Spring runtime injection constructor.
cases.invariant: Discord initiates a private short-lived single-use browser link; credentials and bearer tokens remain at ZezeStudio, only an HMAC-authenticated public platform identity can complete the link, and the ZezeStudio runtime constructor is explicitly marked for Spring injection.
cases.productionSignal: Link issue, completion outcome, expiry/replay/mismatch reason class, and provider name without link code, Discord ID, platform user ID, credentials, or tokens.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A credential or bearer token reaches Discord/Gahyeon, a link is reusable, an invalid signature succeeds, one ZezeStudio identity binds to multiple Gahyeon principals, or the ZezeStudio backend reports a missing default constructor for the link service.

cases.incident: Approval audit rows persisted raw tool arguments, allowing credentials, bearer tokens, and local home-directory identities to enter durable storage.
cases.invariant: Approval matching uses the original argument digest while the durable audit copy recursively redacts sensitive fields, inline secrets, bearer tokens, and user home paths.
cases.productionSignal: Approval outcome, tool name, argument digest, and redaction reason classes without raw tool arguments, credentials, tokens, conversation text, or home paths.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Any credential, token, raw conversation text, or identifiable user home path is persisted in an approval audit row, or redaction prevents an approved original request from being consumed.

cases.incident: Large tool responses could consume the remaining model context without a deterministic size bound or a recoverable reference to the exact original output.
cases.invariant: Small outputs never grow, JSON is compacted losslessly first, and lossy truncation occurs only after the exact original is archived by SHA-256 digest.
cases.productionSignal: Tool name, original character count, compressed character count, compression decision, and output digest without raw tool output.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Compression increases an output, truncates without successfully archiving the exact original, changes a small output, or produces content above the configured bound.

cases.incident: Short or silent audio produced a known phrase the user did not say.
cases.invariant: Known hallucination phrases from short audio are rejected before conversation processing.
cases.productionSignal: Rejected transcription reason and audio duration, without raw user audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Any known hallucination reaches the agent after deployment.

cases.incident: Subsecond audio produced an implausibly long transcript.
cases.invariant: Transcript length must remain plausible for captured audio duration.
cases.productionSignal: Audio duration, transcript length, and guard decision.
cases.rollbackTrigger: An implausible transcript from subsecond audio is accepted.

cases.incident: STT emitted a mechanically repeated token sequence.
cases.invariant: Dominant repeated-token transcripts are rejected regardless of audio length.
cases.productionSignal: Token repetition ratio and guard decision.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A dominant repeated-token transcript reaches the agent.

cases.incident: Internal reasoning or envelope markup appeared in the user-visible response.
cases.invariant: Only the response field of a thought/response envelope is user-visible.
cases.productionSignal: Sanitizer action and output class, without private reasoning content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Internal reasoning or envelope tags become user-visible.

cases.incident: An OpenRouter response beginning with an English conversational reasoning preamble was delivered verbatim to Discord instead of a Korean final answer.
cases.invariant: Known untagged reasoning preambles are rejected as empty final responses and enter the existing bounded corrective retry path.
cases.productionSignal: Reasoning-preamble rejection count, correction count, provider route, and final outcome without prompt, reasoning, or response content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Any model planning, instruction inspection, candidate drafting, or other private reasoning becomes visible or audible to a user.

cases.incident: Sanitization removed the entire model response.
cases.invariant: An empty sanitized response receives exactly one corrective retry.
cases.productionSignal: Empty-final correction count and final outcome.
cases.rollbackTrigger: An empty final response is sent without corrective recovery.

cases.incident: The corrective retry was also empty.
cases.invariant: A safe user-facing fallback is returned when correction remains empty.
cases.productionSignal: Correction exhaustion and fallback selection.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Correction exhaustion produces silence, markup, or an exception.

cases.incident: Piper returned a WAV header without playable speech.
cases.invariant: Header-only audio is rejected as an empty synthesis result.
cases.productionSignal: Synthesized byte length, duration, and rejection reason.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Header-only or zero-duration audio is delivered.

cases.incident: Formatting markup reached speech normalization or produced noise.
cases.invariant: Markup is stripped before transliteration and synthesis.
cases.productionSignal: Normalization outcome class and synthesis success.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Markup is spoken or causes synthesis artifacts.

cases.incident: English terms were pronounced poorly while Korean text was otherwise acceptable.
cases.invariant: Supported English tokens are transliterated, GitHub is passed to Piper as the listener-approved Korean spelling 깃허브 without a raw phoneme override, and Korean text is preserved.
cases.productionSignal: English-token normalization count and fallback count.
cases.rollbackTrigger: GitHub is rewritten to a raw phoneme string, pronounced as 기써브/깃서브, supported English tokens bypass normalization, or Korean text is altered.

cases.incident: Piper joined sentence chunks without a pause, making speech sound rushed and mechanical.
cases.invariant: A configured silence interval is inserted between every pair of synthesized sentence chunks.
cases.productionSignal: Configured sentence-silence response header and synthesized audio duration.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Consecutive sentence chunks are delivered without the configured pause.

cases.incident: The selected Piper voice contained distracting low-frequency and stationary background noise.
cases.invariant: Runtime audio uses the listener-approved high-pass, denoise, and loudness filter chain.
cases.productionSignal: Denoise response header and post-processed WAV validity.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The approved filter chain is absent or produces invalid audio.

cases.incident: Default Piper inference sounded flat and mechanical despite a good voice dataset.
cases.invariant: Runtime synthesis uses the listener-selected length, generator-noise, and phoneme-duration variation values.
cases.productionSignal: Configured inference values and valid synthesized WAV output.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Runtime synthesis falls back to flat default inference values or pronunciation becomes unstable.

cases.incident: The AIRI-style character window exposed a push-to-record button instead of a persistent microphone on/off control.
cases.invariant: Character-window mode exposes a microphone on/off toggle; while enabled, VAD automatically captures each utterance and returns to listening after the response finishes.
cases.testMethod: keeps continuous microphone and TTS controls in the chat window
cases.productionSignal: Desktop microphone control visibility, speech readiness, and transcription outcome without retaining raw audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The character window requires one click per utterance, cannot turn continuous listening off, or bypasses the guarded production STT flow.

cases.incident: The AIRI-style character media loop was silent and moved independently of synthesized speech.
cases.invariant: Character media starts when TTS playback emits avatar.speech.started and returns to its idle frame after avatar.speech.stopped.
cases.testMethod: keeps living-character media moving between speech events
cases.productionSignal: TTS playback start/stop events and character speaking-state transitions.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Audio plays without a speaking animation transition or the speaking loop continues after audio stops.

cases.incident: The packaged Windows preload was emitted as ESM, so Electron rejected it and the renderer sent Core and speech requests to file:///C:/api.
cases.invariant: The sandboxed preload is emitted as preload.cjs, loads the native Core bridge, and never falls back to file-relative API requests in the packaged app.
cases.testMethod: keeps every privileged IPC channel behind the trusted-renderer gate
cases.productionSignal: No preload load error or file:///C:/api request; Core connected; microphone control enabled.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Packaged Electron reports a preload syntax/load error, Core disconnected, or a disabled microphone despite speech readiness.

cases.incident: A personalized news digest could present an unverified single-site report or lose its publication/source evidence.
cases.invariant: Each selected news event is backed by an official source or at least two independent domains, retains publication time and canonical source URLs, and rejects future-dated items.
cases.productionSignal: Per digest: selected event count, official-source flag, distinct source-domain count, and publication age without article body content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A single unverified secondary source is delivered, a source URL/publication time is missing, or a future-dated article is accepted.

cases.incident: A personalized news digest displayed a foreign-language headline and summary without Korean translation.
cases.invariant: Foreign-language personalized news is translated into Korean before formatting, Korean originals are preserved, and failed translations never expose the foreign original.
cases.productionSignal: Per digest: translation attempts, successful translations, skipped translation failures, and delivered event count without article text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A delivered personalized-news title or summary contains an untranslated foreign original, or Korean originals are unnecessarily rewritten.

cases.incident: The assistant claimed it had no real-time news tool when verified recent personalized-news data was already stored internally.
cases.invariant: The agent exposes a read-only recent-news tool that returns validated events in Korean with publication time and canonical sources.
cases.productionSignal: Recent-news tool call count, result class, evidence window, event count, and source count without article body text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A recent-news request claims no tool exists despite qualifying stored events, or returns an event without its publication/source evidence.

cases.incident: A paper request displayed raw tool arguments such as {query: latest AI research papers} instead of a Korean final answer.
cases.invariant: A standalone known tool-argument JSON object is rejected as an empty final response and enters the bounded corrective retry path.
cases.productionSignal: Tool-argument-only rejection count, corrective retry count, and final outcome without argument content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Tool arguments or internal JSON are displayed or spoken as the assistant's final response.

cases.incident: GitHub trending entries without a generated README summary displayed the original English repository description.
cases.invariant: A missing Korean README summary triggers Korean description translation; translation failure omits the description instead of exposing English.
cases.productionSignal: Per campaign: Korean summary hits, description translation attempts/successes/failures, and omitted-description count without README text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: An untranslated English repository description appears in a delivered GitHub trending digest.

cases.incident: Text-channel assistant replies remained silent even while the voice assistant was connected.
cases.invariant: A final text-channel answer is also queued for assistant TTS exactly when that guild has an active voice session; unsafe errors and inactive sessions remain silent.
cases.productionSignal: Text assistant completion followed by assistant TTS synthesis in the same guild without a second AI request.
cases.rollbackTrigger: An active voice session stays silent for a safe text reply, or an inactive session/unsafe error produces audio.

cases.incident: A shared character runtime could leak one character's needs, initiative history, or intentions into another character.
cases.invariant: Life state is keyed by character and world; an event observed by Gahyeon does not mutate Diana's state in the same world.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, world ID, revision, disposition, and reason without private memory contents.
cases.rollbackTrigger: One character's event changes another character's revision, needs, attention, intention, or initiative timestamp.

cases.incident: An autonomous thought loop could speak on every tick or repeat initiatives too frequently.
cases.invariant: Elapsed time normally produces internal change only; cognition requires threshold admission and is suppressed to nonverbal action during cooldown.
cases.productionSignal: Per decision disposition, threshold reason, and cooldown status without generated speech.
cases.rollbackTrigger: An idle tick produces cognition, or a character requests cognition again before its initiative cooldown expires.

cases.incident: A character could record a future intention but forget it before the user returned.
cases.invariant: A prospective intention persists across internal updates and becomes one cognition request when the triggering return event occurs.
cases.productionSignal: Intention presence, trigger type, consumption revision, and disposition without raw private text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The intention disappears before its trigger, fires repeatedly, or is consumed by another character.

cases.incident: Autonomous cognition could read another character's private memories and collapse distinct personalities into one shared agent.
cases.invariant: Every cognition request receives memories from exactly the requested character and world namespace.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, world ID, memory count, and cognition outcome without memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Gahyeon receives Diana's memories, Diana receives Gahyeon's memories, or a world boundary is ignored.

cases.incident: Cognition admission was treated as mandatory speech, causing the character to narrate every internal thought.
cases.invariant: The cognition model can select speak=false, persist a useful reflection, and emit no utterance.
cases.productionSignal: Spoken flag and outcome type without internal reflection content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A speak=false result creates an utterance or every admitted cognition becomes audible speech.

cases.incident: One autonomous provider failure could poison the character loop and prevent later cognition.
cases.invariant: A failed cognition emits a failure outcome without fabricated speech, and a later request can complete normally.
cases.productionSignal: Failure/completion counters by character and provider error class without prompt or memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A provider failure stops future cognition, emits invented speech, or loses the failure signal.

cases.incident: Changing the visible Desktop character left the agent on Gahyeon's system prompt or exposed another character's memory.
cases.invariant: A character-scoped agent session loads only the selected persona and its character/world memory and excludes legacy actor-wide memory.
cases.productionSignal: Selected character ID, world ID, prompt profile ID, and memory count without prompt or memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Diana receives Gahyeon's prompt or memory, a character session reads actor-wide history, or an unknown character silently becomes Gahyeon.

cases.incident: Gahyeon's character prompt was only a few generic sentences, so her identity could collapse into a helpful default assistant or imitate shallow character-chat mannerisms.
cases.invariant: Gahyeon's persona defines a stable identity, relationship-sensitive behavior, conversational rhythm, grounded memory and knowledge use, intentional silence, and anti-dependency boundaries without relying on repeated catchphrases.
cases.productionSignal: Persona profile revision, character ID, response-style bucket, grounded-context presence, and boundary-violation counters without prompt or conversation content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Gahyeon loses her stable identity, exposes relationship scores, invents memories or retrieved facts, repeatedly uses a catchphrase, pressures the user to stay, or cannot choose intentional silence.

cases.incident: Unified knowledge search ranked chunks only by unweighted substring coverage, allowing a recent document with one generic matching term to compete with a document whose title and body matched the complete Korean information need.
cases.invariant: Authorized candidates matching the complete normalized Korean phrase and title terms rank above partial single-term distractors while lexical and semantic scores remain bounded.
cases.productionSignal: Hashed query class, authorized candidate count, title/phrase match buckets, retriever availability, and selected source ID without query or document content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A partial generic-term distractor outranks a complete phrase match, a score leaves 0..1, or an unauthorized source enters ranking.

cases.incident: Character-scoped sessions replaced the legacy system prompt with a persona and therefore lost shared grounding, current-data tool use, failure honesty, and internal-state non-disclosure rules.
cases.invariant: Every selected character combines its isolated persona with identity-neutral shared agent behavior while never inheriting Gahyeon's Discord identity text.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, shared-behavior revision, tool-required decision, and grounding/failure outcome without prompt or conversation content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A character session loses current-data tool guidance, invents tool success, exposes internal state, or receives another character's identity.

cases.incident: Discord rejected characteristic short-audio hallucinations, but the canonical Unreal streaming path accepted any nonblank bounded provider transcript and could forward the same hallucination to the agent.
cases.invariant: Canonical streaming STT measures admitted audio duration and rejects known short-audio hallucinations, implausible transcript lengths, and dominant token repetition before emitting a final transcript.
cases.productionSignal: Hashed stream ID, captured-duration bucket, transcript-shape bucket, rejection reason, and provider class without transcript or audio content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A known short-audio hallucination, impossible-length transcript, or dominant repeated token reaches the Unreal final-transcript sink.

cases.incident: The blind listening builder rejected a completed promotion set containing one objectively selected candidate and the operating baseline, preventing the required two-way human comparison.
cases.invariant: A complete, checksum-verified candidate plus a complete, checksum-verified operating baseline produces a randomized two-label five-prompt blind review without leaking model identity.
cases.productionSignal: Review ID, candidate count, prompt count, checksum verification outcome, and identity-leak validation without model labels or audio content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A one-candidate-plus-baseline completion cannot build, either identity leaks into the page, checksums are bypassed, or the review contains fewer than five matched prompts.

cases.incident: A completed conversation was stored in a shared history instead of the selected character's life memory.
cases.invariant: User and assistant turns are written only to the selected character/world namespace and advance that character's interaction state.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, world ID, stored turn count, and life revision without message content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A Diana conversation appears in Gahyeon's memory, does not update Diana's life state, or is written to the actor-wide legacy history.

cases.incident: The Desktop character changed visually while every response was still synthesized with gahyeon.assistant.
cases.invariant: Every segment in one speech sequence uses the voice profile pinned when the selected character began speaking.
cases.testMethod: pins the selected character voice profile across a speech sequence
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, voice profile ID, segment count, and synthesis status without audio or text content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A Diana sequence uses gahyeon.assistant, segments within one utterance switch voice, or an unvalidated profile reaches Core.

cases.incident: Two users speaking to the same character could receive each other's private memories.
cases.invariant: Personal recall includes only the exact current subject and excludes both unscoped rows and every other subject.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, world ID, subject hash, and recalled count without memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A prompt contains another actor's memory or a character session loses its actor subject scope.

cases.incident: Raw dialogue was treated as permanent memory and repeated processing generated duplicate or low-confidence facts.
cases.invariant: Consolidation emits only supported typed memories, ignores confidence below 0.55, and persists an identical fact once per namespace.
cases.productionSignal: Candidate counts by type, accepted count, deduplicated count, and confidence bucket without memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Low-confidence memory persists, duplicate facts multiply, or an unsupported memory type is admitted.

cases.incident: A future intention was stored in the database but never affected the character when the user returned.
cases.invariant: A pending prospective intention changes the next completed interaction into user.returned, allowing the Life Policy to consume it once for cognition.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, intention-present flag, user-returned trigger, and consumption revision without intention content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A pending intention receives only user.interaction, never triggers cognition, or fires repeatedly after consumption.

cases.incident: Recent low-value chatter displaced old but important preferences, while expired working memory remained recallable.
cases.invariant: Recall ranks importance, confidence, emotional weight, type-specific decay, and recency while excluding expired memory.
cases.productionSignal: Memory type, age bucket, score bucket, expiry status, and rank without memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Expired working memory is recalled or recent trivial chatter displaces a high-confidence durable preference.

cases.incident: Contradicting semantic facts accumulated side by side, allowing the agent to claim both were currently true.
cases.invariant: A stable memoryKey has one active value per namespace; weaker contradictions are rejected and competitive evidence supersedes without deleting history.
cases.productionSignal: Memory key hash, old/new confidence buckets, merge result, and active-count without memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Two values for one topic remain active, weaker evidence replaces stronger evidence, or superseded history is deleted.

cases.incident: Trust or tension learned by one character with one user leaked into another character or user relationship.
cases.invariant: Relationship state is keyed by character, world, and actor subject, and positive/negative evidence updates bounded dimensions independently.
cases.productionSignal: Namespace IDs, revision, and bucketed familiarity/trust/affinity/tension without memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Evidence changes another namespace, a dimension leaves 0..1, or negative evidence increases trust.

cases.incident: Persistent relationship values existed in storage but never changed how the selected character generated a response.
cases.invariant: The selected character and actor relationship state is included in the system context without exposing another relationship.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, actor subject hash, relationship revision, and value buckets without prompt content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The agent omits current relationship state, reads another user's state, or narrates raw numeric values to the user.

cases.incident: A cognition expression plan was discarded and the utterance was synthesized in the same neutral voice regardless of context.
cases.invariant: Style, continuous intensity, communicative intent, and voice identity cross Desktop and Core unchanged; an unavailable expressive provider fails closed instead of silently using neutral TTS.
cases.productionSignal: Character ID, voice profile, bounded style, intensity bucket, provider readiness, and synthesis outcome without text or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Expression controls disappear, an expressive request reaches neutral synthesis, or unavailable expressive TTS returns a successful neutral voice.

cases.incident: A remote expressive worker could return audio from the wrong speaker, model, or quantization while Core treated it as the requested Gahyeon voice.
cases.invariant: Every Qwen response attests the exact voice profile, model ID, and quantization requested by Core and returns bounded PCM WAV bytes.
cases.productionSignal: Expected and observed identity hashes, model ID, quantization, byte count, media contract, latency, and outcome without audio or text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A mismatched speaker/model/quantization is accepted, non-WAV audio is admitted, or the response exceeds the configured byte limit.

cases.incident: Core startup failed because a multi-constructor expression planning service did not identify its Spring runtime injection constructor.
cases.invariant: Every multi-constructor Spring life or expression component explicitly annotates its runtime injection constructor.
cases.productionSignal: Core application context reaches ready state and the expression planner bean is constructed without recording user content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Core startup reports a missing default constructor or cannot construct the conversation expression planner.

cases.incident: A retired Electron compatibility client was launched and presented as the actual macOS character service.
cases.invariant: Service launch selects only the canonical Unreal runtime; retired Electron launch and packaging commands fail closed, and an unpromoted Unreal runtime cannot be substituted with another surface.
cases.productionSignal: Selected runtime, manifest status, Unreal project/map identity, and launcher outcome without user content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Electron launches or packages as the service, or any legacy/diagnostic surface is shown after the canonical Unreal launcher refuses readiness.

cases.incident: Qwen3-TTS 1.7B reached ROCm inference on zeze but HIP launch failures wedged the Radeon 780M; an official PyTorch BF16 attempt also caused system OOM, restarted production Java pods, and forced an amdgpu reset.
cases.invariant: A zeze Qwen runtime is never promoted when synthesis evidence contains a HIP launch failure, GPU reset, recovered-wedged-device signal, system OOM, or production process termination.
cases.productionSignal: Runtime build identity, accelerator architecture, exit status, generated token count, latency, kernel reset/OOM markers, and privacy-safe pod restart counts without prompt text or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Any HIP launch failure, amdgpu reset, device-wedged event, system OOM, production pod restart, missing qualifying traffic, or synthesis process termination blocks promotion and keeps the existing endpoint unchanged.

cases.incident: A direct request to laugh produced a capability disclaimer and was flattened through neutral custom TTS instead of audible expression.
cases.invariant: Direct laughter requests produce a suppressed_laugh expression and can reach only a ready expressive provider; neutral fallback fails closed.
cases.productionSignal: Voice profile, style, intensity bucket, provider readiness, model attestation, latency, and outcome without transcript or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A laughter request emits a capability disclaimer, reaches neutral TTS, loses its expression controls, or succeeds without provider attestation.

cases.incident: Short voice actions and gratitude received repetitive multi-sentence offers of help instead of a direct natural response.
cases.invariant: Voice greetings, gratitude, and short action requests are answered in one sentence, and direct sound actions are performed without capability disclaimers.
cases.productionSignal: Voice modality, response sentence-count bucket, action-request class, and sanitizer outcome without response text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A short voice action produces a disclaimer or help-offer loop, or a simple acknowledgement exceeds one sentence.

cases.incident: The shared Unreal voice component compiled on macOS but the Diana runtime could not enable its private begin-play capture flag, leaving STT without microphone audio.
cases.invariant: The canonical macOS Unreal launcher explicitly opts into microphone capture and the shared Stage component honors that runtime argument without reintroducing Electron.
cases.productionSignal: Runtime platform, audio-capture implementation, microphone-start outcome, STT mode, and failure reason without PCM or transcript content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The macOS runtime starts without the microphone argument, AudioCapture has no platform implementation, Electron returns, or capture fails to open a device.

cases.incident: The Qwen cutover image entered CrashLoopBackOff because PCM streaming configuration required the Unreal TTS executor while the Unreal WebSocket runtime was disabled.
cases.invariant: PCM stream caching is created only when both the headless and Unreal WebSocket runtimes are enabled; Discord-only Qwen deployments start without an Unreal executor.
cases.productionSignal: Application readiness, Unreal WebSocket enablement, PCM cache activation, and missing-bean failure class without transcript or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: The replacement Pod fails readiness, reports a missing unrealTtsExecutor bean, or PCM streaming activates while the Unreal WebSocket runtime is disabled.

cases.incident: The canonical macOS Unreal companion shipped only placement controls while Windows exposed chat, microphone/STT, speaker/TTS, and character model selection.
cases.invariant: The native macOS Unreal overlay retains transparent character controls and exposes a native control center with chat, STT, TTS, character selection, Core readiness, placement, scale, yaw, and reset without reviving Electron.
cases.productionSignal: Runtime identity, Core reachability, STT/TTS readiness flags, selected character ID, and control action outcome without transcript, audio, or message content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Electron is launched, transparency or animation regresses, a control silently does nothing, Core errors are hidden, or chat/STT/TTS/model controls disappear from the native macOS overlay.

cases.incident: The pre-hardening character-memory fallback admitted subject-null rows during personalized recall and represented every caller only as a local actor ID, leaving canonical account continuity and strict per-user exclusion incomplete.
cases.invariant: Every durable personal-memory read is filtered by character, world, and an exact non-null subject; linked accounts use the immutable ZezeStudio UUID, unlinked known principals remain in isolated provisional namespaces, and explicitly uncertain speakers have no persistent memory context.
cases.productionSignal: Hashed subject namespace class, character/world scope, persistence class, filtered candidate count, and recall outcome without UUIDs, conversation text, or memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A recall returns a null-subject or different-subject row, an uncertain speaker is persisted, a linked account does not resolve to the attested ZezeStudio UUID namespace, or a pre-link namespace is merged without explicit approval.

cases.incident: Before the integrated knowledge layer, domain RAG stores were separate and there was no generic document ingestion path with mandatory service and subject authorization before ranking.
cases.invariant: Knowledge ingestion is content-idempotent, private chunks are retrieved only for the exact service and owner subject, and authorization filtering occurs in SQL before lexical or semantic ranking.
cases.productionSignal: Service ID, access-scope class, hashed subject class, authorized candidate count, ranking mode, and result count without document or query text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A private chunk is returned to another subject or service, ranking evaluates an unauthorized candidate, duplicate ingestion creates a second document, or a deleted source remains recallable.

cases.incident: The first V41 disposable PostgreSQL boot reached a valid migrated schema but Core failed because the multi-constructor KnowledgeBaseService did not identify its Spring runtime injection constructor.
cases.invariant: KnowledgeBaseService has exactly one runtime constructor explicitly annotated for Spring injection while retaining its package-private clock-injected test constructor.
cases.productionSignal: Application startup outcome, bean class, migration version, and failure class without database credentials, knowledge text, or user identifiers.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Core reports a missing default constructor, cannot instantiate KnowledgeBaseService, or fails after V41 migration before readiness.

cases.incident: Account linking previously had no governed workflow for moving provisional personal memories to the canonical ZezeStudio UUID namespace.
cases.invariant: Only an owned principal namespace can merge into its linked ZezeStudio UUID, and no memory or relationship row moves before a single explicit approval proof is durably hashed.
cases.productionSignal: Merge request ID, namespace classes, state transition, approval digest presence, and moved row counts without raw proof, UUID, or memory content.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Any pre-link memory moves without APPROVED state, a target is not linked to the principal, raw approval proof is persisted, or cross-principal namespaces merge.

cases.incident: Personal data deletion had no single auditable operation spanning relational memories, derived knowledge, external vectors, and caches.
cases.invariant: An authorized deletion job removes subject data from PostgreSQL and derived rows, invokes every configured vector and cache deletion port, and records per-layer completion before declaring success.
cases.productionSignal: Deletion job ID, hashed subject class, per-layer completion booleans, deleted row count, and failure class without UUID, memory content, or conversation text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A job reports COMPLETED while a configured deletion layer did not run, an unauthorized principal deletes another subject, or any subject-owned relational or derived row remains.

cases.incident: The Qwen 1.7B concerned style averaged -35.6 dB while the natural style averaged -24.2 dB, making concerned speech difficult to hear.
cases.invariant: The approved concerned profile applies a bounded 3.72 output gain to WAV and streaming PCM while leaving every other expression unchanged and clipping safely to signed 16-bit limits.
cases.productionSignal: Attested model/profile identity, style, output-gain bucket, clipped-sample count bucket, latency, and synthesis outcome without text, audio, or user identifier.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Concerned output is materially quieter than natural speech, clips audibly, causes synthesis failures or latency regression, or any non-concerned style receives output gain.

cases.incident: Production speech remained on Piper or the legacy zeze Vulkan Qwen endpoint, so the approved concerned loudness correction deployed to the land CUDA bridge received zero requests.
cases.invariant: The zeze Core expressive route targets the attested land Qwen 1.7B CUDA bridge at 10.42.0.1:18773 with c-int4-cuda-sm75-mixed while standard non-expressive speech retains its approved provider.
cases.productionSignal: Provider class, style, endpoint port, model and quantization attestation, HTTP outcome, latency, and audio byte-count bucket without transcript, audio, API key, or user identifier.
cases.rollbackTrigger: Expressive traffic returns to port 18771 or Vulkan attestation, port 18773 receives no qualifying expressive request while another provider speaks it, or the corrected route increases synthesis failures beyond the canary threshold.

cases.incident: A Korean voice conversation produced an unsolicited English final answer that was accepted as speakable output.
cases.invariant: Voice answers default to Korean and switch languages only when the user explicitly requests it, while preserving original English spellings for technical terms and names.
cases.productionSignal: Voice modality, requested-language class, response-language class, and policy revision without transcript or response text.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A Korean voice request produces a predominantly non-Korean answer without an explicit language request, or requested English terms are forcibly transliterated.

cases.incident: Gahyeon's own recently played speech was recaptured through a user's microphone, admitted as a new request, and stopped the active TTS track mid-sentence.
cases.invariant: A recent high-similarity echo of bot speech is rejected before revision increment and playback interruption, while semantically different user speech remains eligible for barge-in.
cases.productionSignal: Guild, hashed speaker class, transcript length bucket, similarity bucket, echo-window bucket, and admission outcome without transcript or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A likely self-echo increments the response revision or stops TTS, or a clearly different meaningful user utterance is suppressed as echo.

cases.incident: The Discord voice expression policy recognized only laughter and gratitude, so requests for a worried tone never selected the corrected concerned Qwen profile.
cases.invariant: Concern and anxiety requests select the bounded concerned expression, and explicit English-pronunciation requests carry a pronunciation intent to the expressive provider.
cases.productionSignal: Hashed intent class, selected style, intensity bucket, provider readiness, and synthesis outcome without transcript or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: A concern request remains natural, an English-pronunciation request loses its intent, or an unsupported style reaches synthesis.

cases.incident: English and mixed Korean-English output was always sent to the Qwen runtime with Korean language control, producing Koreanized English pronunciation.
cases.invariant: The Qwen bridge selects English for English-dominant text, Auto for mixed Korean-English text, and Korean otherwise without logging or persisting text.
cases.productionSignal: Language class, style, character-count buckets, model attestation, latency, and outcome without text or audio.
cases.rollbackTrigger: English-dominant text is synthesized in Korean mode, Korean text unexpectedly switches language, or speaker identity attestation changes.
